questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had already lived in Paris for a year, and completed an internship at the Danish embassy in Paris as a part of my education. I wanted to continue to live here and combine it with studies, and therefore I applied to Sorbonne.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: To be honest, it was not easy at all and I don't think the different systems communicate well. It is difficult both to find information at your home university, at the host university and from Erasmus. And there is no overall "guide" to how you proceed - you are very much on your own.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Actually, almost nothing. The administration at Sorbonne functions very poorly, and it is very difficult to receive assistance from the regarding anything. It seems like they are not used to the processes around exchange students. First of all knowing who to contact was difficult to find out, and when you found them, the assistance they provided were very slow and not very helpful. Again, you are very much on your own. There is an introduction day for exchange students at the beginning, but this is much more about being an Erasmus student in a new city, how to take the subway, social events etc. It doesn't provide you with the necessary information about how you choose courses, which courses are available to you, when the courses begin, examination, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had lived in Paris already for a year so therefore it was not a problem for me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive and you have to start looking very much in advance !

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process is honestly a mess! It is super difficult to navigate in, you are provided with little to no information, it is difficult to know who to reach out to, and it doesn't appear as they know it either. I took me more than a month from when school started in September until I was properly registered, which was very stressful and frustrating.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is different offices (UFRs) connected to the different Masters at Sorbonne's Faculty des Lettres, but they communicate bad with each other, the systems are poor, and it doesn't seem as if the people who work there are sure of the processes either. So very little help - you have to consult with other students, write many many e-mails to the administration etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: After a month I succeeded, but it was the most difficult, complicated, and confusing process. The teachers don't communicate with the administration, and no one has any information about which and how many courses are available to Erasmus students in relation to their home university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start the process very very early and be consistent and stubborn in writing to the administration regarding the information you need. If they don't reply, you have to go there physically and ask the questions about the registration and maybe even see them register you on their own computer, so you are sure it is completed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses is fine I think - I studied philosophy which I don't do at home so for me it was of course difficult because it was new to me. What is very different from my home university is the large amount of courses you have to take at Sorbonne to get it to add up to the mandatory 30 ECTS points. This means that there are a lot to manage, a lot of information to take in and learn and especially a lot of exams. So even though the level of the courses is appropriate the large amount of courses and exams are too overwhelming, I think.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is much more old school and they don't practice active style of teaching as we are used to. It is a lecture; the professor lectures and the students listen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you study political science - as I do - I think these are the best alternatives within the Master in Political philosophy. The only one not super relevant to our field is philosophie morale, as it is more a course in ethics and moral philosophy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is expensive in Paris. The rent is high if you want to find housing off campus. It is not unexpected but there are a lot of costs combined with living as a student in Paris.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is less expensive than I expected, and people do it a lot!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think quite a few, but I never participated in it, so I don't know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I never tried them, so I can't recommend any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It depends on what you want to get out of the stay and how well you know the city. For me, I had already lived here for a long time, so I just "continued with my life". If you are only here for the exchange I recommend you get the most out of the city; experience museums, nice restaurants, walk around to see the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I was already familiar with the French culture, so for me it was easy. If you are not used to this, I think a French university can be very tough. It is much more formal and oldschool than I imagine it is in a lot of other countries.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Unfortunately, no. I was already settled with a group of friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Being Danish you have to watch out for the frequent use of irony and sarcasm, as it doesn't always fit into the French culture and way of socializing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the culture around restaurants and bars; the social life in Paris in all age groups I think is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Start researching and planning as early as possible! Look in the course catalogues, reach out to the administration, find housing etc. 
- Be aware of the language barrier! Even if you passed the French language test (B2) be aware that EVERYTHING is in French, the professors are often bad at English, and the French teaching level is high 
- Reach out to our professors in the beginning of the semester stating that you are an Erasmus student so they are aware - my teachers were very nice in regard to this because I had told them from the beginning

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that a lot of exams are completed in hand writing at the university as a table top exercise, which we are not used to in Copenhagen. Thus, practice writing and taking notes in handwriting from the beginning.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To complete so many courses in French within a field I have never studied before.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language and the administration

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
